title: THE SAME WELCOME AT THE ALTAR

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'He shall tear it open by the wings, not dividing it completely, and then the priest shall burn it on the wood that is burning on the altar. It is a burnt offering, a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD.'" - Lev 1:17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
For the third time in this chapter, the same closing verdict: an aroma pleasing to the LORD. It was said over the bull. It was said over the lamb. Now it is said over a small bird brought by someone with nothing else to give.

That is how Leviticus 1 ends — not with a hierarchy of worshippers, but with one word of acceptance spoken three times over three very different gifts.

This is the heart of God on display before a single law about clean and unclean has been given. Before the priesthood is ordained. Before the Day of Atonement. God's first word to His redeemed people is: here is how you may come, and here is how I will receive you.

And it all pointed to one final offering. The writer of Hebrews says that these sacrifices could never take away sins, being repeated endlessly year after year — but Christ offered for all time one sacrifice for sins and sat down (Heb 10:11-12). The fire on that altar burned continually because the work was never finished. His work is.

You come to God now not with a bull or a bird, but in the name of the One who was Himself the offering, and who is pleasing to the Father forever.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live as though Christ's sacrifice is finished, or as though I must keep adding to it?
2. What would change today if I truly believed God receives me with delight in Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are the offering that never needs repeating. I come to the Father through You alone, and I thank You that His welcome is complete. Amen.
